32.author: St. John Chrysostom
32.work: Homilies on the Acts of the Apostles, Homily 11
32.text: Chrysostom returns again and again to the verse 'the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul.' He notices that Luke does not say they were of one belief and one teaching. That had been said a few verses earlier. He says one heart and one soul. The doctrine joined them at the head; the love joined them at the depth. Chrysostom asks his Antiochene congregation what has happened to the second part. The first is preached every Sunday; the second has nearly disappeared. He does not soften the verdict.

32.author: St. Basil the Great
32.text: Basil reads Acts 4:32 as the apostolic charter of his cenobitic monasticism. The pattern of the first community in Jerusalem, where no one called any of his possessions his own, was not given for the first generation only; it was given as the original form of Christian life, to which the monastic vocation returns. Married Christians cannot live it fully; the monastery, Basil says, is the place where the verse is taken at its word.
